clue.text: Adolescent boys are often so irregular

definitions.meaning: teenage boys are often afflicted with acne, covered in pimples

explanation.surface: A remark about teenage boys being unpredictable in their behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Patchy or uneven performance is described with the same word as a pimpled face, a synonym for inconsistent.

clue.text: Arrange to come down on heretic, a worm

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece lands on top of the second

parts.note: to plan is to arrange
an Arian followed the heretic Arius

explanation.surface: Someone plans to come down hard on a heretic, called a worm.
explanation.definitionFit: A planarian is a flatworm, an example of a worm.

clue.text: Get into air strip

definitions.meaning: become airborne, as a plane leaving the runway

explanation.surface: Getting a plane airborne from a runway.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane leaving the ground is airborne, and to undress is to remove clothing; one phrase covers both.

clue.text: Even now you may be on time

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: Even now you may arrive punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: Yet means still or up to this moment, a synonym for even now.

clue.text: Thin material, but order me a gross

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a gross of a flimsy fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a request to buy, but it signals rearranging MEAGROSS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer is a very fine, filmy fabric, so it is an example of thin material.

clue.text: Marker finally inserted in some DNA in style

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a gene is a section of DNA

indicators.note: only the end letter of the word is wanted

explanation.surface: A genetic marker is spliced into a strand of DNA.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a kind or category of art, a synonym for style.

clue.text: Seeing back, have a stab — criticise afterwards

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it
to guess is to attempt an answer

explanation.surface: With hindsight someone tries a guess and then finds fault.
explanation.definitionFit: To second-guess is to judge or question a decision with hindsight, so to find fault after the event.

clue.text: New Arab actor who's poor as patriarch

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a ham is a bad overacting performer

explanation.surface: A new Arab actor plays a poor role as a patriarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham is the Old Testament father of the Hebrew people, an example of a patriarch.

clue.text: Frame from which animal popped head out

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a weasel is an animal

explanation.surface: An animal poked its head out of a frame.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Pop Goes the Weasel.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand for holding a painting, an example of a frame.

clue.text: Fill a single container, and stop

parts.note: to pack is to fill
I is the Roman numeral one
a tin is a container

explanation.surface: Instructions to fill one container and then halt.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for quitting something altogether is a synonym of stop.

clue.text: Dancer is exhibiting clothing — red

indicators.note: the clue words wrap around the answer like clothes around a body

explanation.surface: A dancer shows off a red costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' looks like the dancer's costume, but it says the words Dancer is exhibiting enclose the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerise is a cherry-coloured shade, an example of red.

clue.text: The Irish love to hold wake, clutching Bible even

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it, as a hand clutches

parts.note: to hold a wake is to mourn the dead
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
e'en is a poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: An Irish lover sits vigil over the dead while holding a Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: E'EN is a poetic contraction a solver may not know; 'clutching' puts the Authorised Version's abbreviation inside the word for holding a wake.
explanation.definitionFit: Mavourneen is an Irish term of endearment meaning my darling, a word for a loved one.

clue.text: Feeble performer with puppet gets the chop

parts.note: rabbit is British sporting slang for a poor player, especially a tailend batsman
Punch is the puppet of Punch and Judy

explanation.surface: A weak performer and a puppet are fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the chop' looks like being sacked, but the chop is a blow to the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbit punch is a chopping blow to the back of the neck, a sense of chop.

clue.text: Complete, except at the front there's a gap

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word is left out

parts.note: whole means complete

explanation.surface: Something is finished apart from a gap at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole is an opening, a synonym for gap.

clue.text: Listened to' section of book gladly once

indicators.note: what is listened to is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a leaf is a page of a book

explanation.surface: A section of a book that someone gladly heard read aloud long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Lief is an archaic word meaning willingly, so it fits gladly in old usage.

clue.text: Encourage deception in dicey con-. test

parts.note: to back someone is to support or encourage them
gammon is old slang for humbug or deceit

explanation.surface: Someone eggs on cheating in a game of chance.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan splits contest across a line as con-. test; it is one word. GAMMON for nonsense or deceit is old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game played with dice, so it is a contest of chance.

clue.text: Bloke can't finish drink

indicators.note: the end letter of the word is lost

parts.note: chap means bloke

explanation.surface: A man cannot finish his drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cha is British slang for tea, an example of a drink.

clue.text: Badly miss actor, transferring to — Coventry?

indicators.note: something done badly is messed up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sorely misses an actor who has transferred to a Coventry theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: To send someone to Coventry is a British idiom for refusing to speak to them; Coventry is a city in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending a person to Coventry means shunning them, which is exclusion from society.

clue.text: I plan finally to speak about noise that's excessive

indicators.note: only the end letter of the word is wanted
one word goes around another

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally
din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A plan to speak out about excessive noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Inordinate means beyond reasonable limits, a synonym for excessive.

clue.text: Crash into section in wall

parts.note: to ram is to crash into
a part is a section

explanation.surface: Something crashes into a section of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampart is a defensive embankment or wall around a fort.

clue.text: Prepares for short bouts

definitions.meaning: to fit someone for a task is to prepare or equip them
sudden attacks, as of coughing or temper

explanation.surface: Someone gets ready for brief contests.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitting out is equipping or preparing, and seizures or spells of temper are short sudden episodes.

clue.text: Prudence heard this family saga

indicators.note: the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: foresight is prudence about the future

explanation.surface: A woman called Prudence listened to a family saga.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prudence' looks like a woman's name. The Forsyte Saga is Galsworthy's novel sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forsyte family are the subject of Galsworthy's Forsyte Saga novels.

clue.text: Resolute backing provided by troops at sea

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the word that follows it is read from right to left

parts.note: if means provided that
RM is the Royal Marines, soldiers who serve with the navy

explanation.surface: Determined support from marines.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means steadfast and unwavering, a synonym for resolute.

clue.text: Goad politician into lie in broadcast

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another
something broadcast is scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician is provoked into lying on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scrambles the word lie to give IEL, and 'into' places the politician inside those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or urge forward, a synonym for goad.

clue.text: Unexpectedly ran despite being lame

indicators.note: something unexpected happens out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lame person surprisingly managed to run.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian in the sense of dull and uninspired matches lame meaning feeble or weak.

clue.text: Going down, he may be protected by the bell.

definitions.text: Going down, he may be protected by the bell.

parts.words: Going down, he may be protected by the bell.
parts.note: reads like a boxer saved by the bell when knocked down, but describes someone descending under water in a diving bell

explanation.surface: A boxer on the canvas is saved by the bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone working underwater may descend in a diving bell, a chamber that protects them.

clue.text: Minor injury from run in the country

indicators.note: one piece sits inside another

parts.note: Spain is a country
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone hurts an ankle running in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' looks like rural land but is a nation, SPAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprain is a wrenched joint or ligament, an example of a minor injury.

clue.text: From girl, invocation to be God's servant

parts.note: Val is a girl's name
the Kyrie is the prayer Lord, have mercy

explanation.surface: A girl prays to become a servant of God.
explanation.definitionFit: Valkyries were handmaidens of Odin in Norse myth, so a servant of a god.

clue.text: Cover most of open-air pool

indicators.note: the final letter is left off

parts.note: a lido is an outdoor swimming pool

explanation.surface: Covering most of an outdoor swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lid is a top that covers a container.

clue.text: Old playwright put engraver on floor

indicators.note: one piece is placed after the other

parts.note: an etcher engraves metal plates

explanation.surface: An engraver is laid out on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: John Fletcher was a Jacobean playwright who collaborated with Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: John Fletcher wrote plays in the early seventeenth century, an example of an old dramatist.

clue.text: Misty, like a midsummer night?

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's comedy is A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A hazy midsummer evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamy means vague or hazy, and the Shakespeare title links a midsummer night with sleep-visions.
